stories.title: Gartner survey: only 13% of companies see real AI returns
stories.summary: A Gartner survey of 2,002 CIOs found only 13 percent of companies see real business value from AI investments, even as most plan to keep raising tech budgets.
stories.more: The survey also found 51 percent of respondents expect AI to actually increase their operating costs rather than cut them. Despite the thin returns, 75 percent of CEOs plan to keep raising their technology budgets, suggesting strategic conviction in AI is currently outpacing measurable results.

items.title: Only 13 percent of companies see real returns from AI, Gartner survey finds
items.excerpt: Only 13 percent of companies are getting real business value from their AI investments, according to a Gartner survey of 2,002 CIOs. At the same time, 51 percent expect AI to actually increase their operating costs. Yet 75 percent of CEOs plan to keep raising their technology budgets. So far, strategic conviction is beating measurable results. The article Only 13 percent of companies see real returns from AI, Gartner survey finds appeared first on The Decoder .

stories.title: Laika's Wildwood director calls AI 'antithetical' to the stop-motion studio
stories.summary: Travis Knight, director of Laika's new film Wildwood, says AI is 'antithetical to everything we are' at the studio, which built the film using over 230 puppets.
stories.more: Wildwood is Laika's most ambitious film yet, a sprawling fantasy adventure that took five years to complete. Production used more than 230 puppets, including 36 versions of the main character Prue alone. Director Travis Knight frames the studio's handcrafted, puppet-based process as fundamentally opposed to AI-driven approaches to filmmaking.

stories.title: DeepSeek reportedly raises $15B days after US tech restrictions
stories.summary: Chinese AI lab DeepSeek has reportedly raised $15 billion, one of China's largest funding rounds, just days after the US ordered federal agencies to drop its technology.
stories.more: The reported $15 billion round would rank among the largest funding deals in China to date. It comes just days after the US government ordered federal agencies to remove DeepSeek's technology, citing national security concerns, highlighting the tension between US restrictions and continued investor interest in the company.

stories.title: Recursive unveils Flint, a 40B-parameter coding model from its Eureka Machine
stories.summary: AI startup Recursive, founded by former DeepMind researchers, released Flint, a 40-billion-parameter MoE model for local coding, built in four months using its in-house 'Eureka Machine.'
stories.more: Flint is a 40-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts model aimed at local coding use cases. It was developed in about four months using Recursive's in-house system, the Eureka Machine, which independently tests and optimizes model architectures. Recursive, founded by former DeepMind researchers, says Flint is the first public result of this AI-driven research process. The company has yet to demonstrate whether the approach can scale into genuinely self-improving AI.

stories.title: Claude did not invent scorpion antivenom, despite investment firm's AI drug test
stories.summary: Investment firm Citrini Research partnered with Anthropic to test whether an unreleased Claude model could design scorpion antivenom; it produced only early leads, not a working drug.
stories.more: Citrini Research set out to show AI could revolutionize drug development by having an unreleased version of Claude attempt to design scorpion antivenom. The model came up with some promising starting points but nothing close to an actual drug, according to experts who reviewed the work for The Verge. The episode is cited as a cautionary example against overstating what current AI models can do in specialized scientific domains like drug discovery.

stories.title: PrismaCoder paper aims to close the gap in open multimodal code models
stories.summary: A new paper, PrismaCoder, proposes a decomposed rubric synthesis method to narrow the gap between open and proprietary multimodal code models.
stories.more: Multimodal code intelligence spans generating visual outputs like charts, webpages, animations, and semi-structured documents directly from code execution. Proprietary models have advanced quickly at turning a text description or screenshot into interactive artifacts, but their training data and methods stay closed. PrismaCoder introduces a decomposed rubric synthesis approach aimed at giving open models comparable capability. The paper argues open progress has mainly been held back by the quantity and quality of available training data.

stories.title: AI shopping agents are ready to buy, but some retailers are blocking them
stories.summary: AI shopping agents, marketed as personal assistants, are being blocked or restricted by some retailers including Amazon, The RealReal, and Target.
stories.more: Tech companies have pitched AI shopping agents as personal assistants that bring concierge-level help to ordinary shoppers. In practice, the experience is described as closer to sending an anxious, apologetic teenager to shop on your behalf. Retailers including Amazon, The RealReal, Target, and Meta's Muse have reportedly blocked or restricted these agents from completing purchases on their sites.

stories.title: OpenAI, Anthropic, and Nvidia post record lobbying spending in Q3
stories.summary: Anthropic, OpenAI, and Nvidia each logged their highest-ever quarterly lobbying spend between July and September, with Nvidia leading at $2.2 million.
stories.more: Federal disclosures show Nvidia spent $2.2 million on lobbying in the quarter, followed by Anthropic at $2.1 million and OpenAI at $1.5 million. All three posted their highest-spending lobbying quarter to date. The Verge notes this outpaces other Big Tech firms with longer-established presences in Washington, pointing to an increasingly active push by AI companies to shape policy.

stories.title: PHP2Shell flaw puts huge swaths of the web at risk
stories.summary: Two vulnerabilities in PHP, nicknamed PHP2Shell, endanger a large share of the web; hackers reportedly began probing the bug four days before defenders were told it existed.
stories.more: PHP powers an estimated 70 percent of websites, including Wikipedia, WordPress, and Drupal, making the two newly disclosed vulnerabilities, dubbed PHP2Shell, especially far-reaching. Some affected sites, including DeviantArt and 4chan, were temporarily taken offline as a precaution. Security researchers say hackers were already probing the flaw roughly four days before it was publicly disclosed, giving defenders a late start on patching.
